transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-03 15:00 PST
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Recorder: Fireflies.ai
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO, Cobalt Delta), Ethan Kim (Head of ML), Rosa Martinez (Platform), Samir Basu (Security)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be noisy): Redwood demo/assessment, migration checklist, discuss private deployment.

--- Transcript Body ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have most folks here. Quick intros?
[00:08] Priya Nair: Yeah hi Priya here, CTO at Cobalt Delta, we own the LLM stack decision, thanks for setting this up.
[00:13] Ethan Kim: Ethan, head of ML. We've been piloting OpenAI and running a bunch of vLLM hosts on-prem, trying to figure out cost and output drift.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Awesome, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and Liam and Anika are our SEs who will dig into the technical bits.
[00:26] Liam O'Connor: Hi all, Liam, I focus on runtime and batching/kv-cache behaviours.
[00:30] Rosa Martinez: Rosa, platform eng, I manage the k8s clusters and infra for the on-prem vllm stuff.
[00:34] Samir Basu: Samir, security, I'll ask the compliance-y questions.

[00:40] Maya Chen: Cool, Geraldean plan for the next 45 mins: we want to understand your current environment, must-haves for migration, and outline next steps. Priya, can you start with high level?
[00:49] Priya Nair: Sure. We've been using OpenAI for prod user-facing flows but we're seeing rising cost and less deterministic latency. We spun up vLLM on some NVMe boxes to reduce cost and control data, but results are mixed. Tokenization differences, occasional hallucinations, and some function-calling edge cases - plus the team is stretched operating those clusters. We're evaluating Redwood for either hosted (to reduce ops) or Dedicated / Private for compliance.
[01:12] Maya Chen: Nice, makes sense. Ethan, from an ML eval POV what are your blockers?
[01:16] Ethan Kim: The big one is eval parity—our product has downstream scoring and we can't accept regressions. We use golden prompt sets to validate outputs and we also test streaming and function-calling integration. vLLM/TGI variants sometimes respond slightly differently to OpenAI. We need a way to replicate OpenAI semantics or at least measure and accept differences.
[01:34] Liam O'Connor: On the runtime side, vllm and TGI have different KV cache semantics and chunking behaviour which affects latency and context window effectiveness. Redwood's runtime exposes KV cache controls and prefix caching; we also have quantized execution paths.
[01:47] Rosa Martinez: When you say quantized, do you mean you do 4-bit int8--like I'm sorry--some of our stuff uses 4-bit Q4, some Q8, and we saw big latency differences.
[01:56] Anika Rao: Right, we support multiple quantization profiles, and our Recommend engine will suggest profiles per model and workload. For example, Q4_0 vs Q8_0 has different throughput/latency tradeoffs; we can run your prompt set to recommend.
[02:09] Samir Basu: Security first — do you have VPC/private deployments? We process PHI and need strict controls. SOC2? KMS integration?
[02:17] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer VPC deployment and on-prem options; we support KMS integrations and offer audit logs and SAML/SSO with RBAC. We're SOC 2 Type II and have ISO docs we can share.
[02:27] Samir Basu: Good. Also curious about audit log granularity and retention options.
[02:33] Tomás Alvarez: We can export detailed per-request logs, token counts, latency traces and map to request IDs; retention is configurable per plan.

[02:40] Ethan Kim: Back to parity — how do you handle differences between model formats? We have models trained in HF format, some fine-tuned with Anthropic tooling. Will Redwood preserve exact tokenizer behaviour, function calling schema, and stop sequences?
[02:54] Liam O'Connor: Great question. We support Hugging Face format and common tokenizers. There are edge cases where tokenizers diverge; our onboarding checks tokenization and normalizes streaming semantics. For function calling we emulate OpenAI-compatible RPCs and support tool-calling with structured JSON outputs. But sometimes model-level fine-tunes produce different output distributions; that's why the eval benchmark is important.
[03:15] Priya Nair: What about prompt engineering differences? We have a set of system prompts that rely on subtle behaviour from OpenAI chat completions. Will those translate 1:1?
[03:23] Anika Rao: Usually the system-message semantics do translate but you may see small shifts. We recommend running a parity suite which runs your exact prompt set against (a) OpenAI baseline, (b) Redwood-hosted same model variant if available, (c) Redwood Dedicated with quantization profiles, (d) on-prem vLLM if you want.

[03:43] Rosa Martinez: Our latency SLO is 250ms p95 for short completion flows. OpenAI usually meets that, but when we self-host with vLLM p95 spikes. Can Redwood meet 250ms p95?
[03:53] Liam O'Connor: For short context and smaller models, yes on Dedicated with appropriate GPU sizing and batching. Hosted depends on plan/region—our hosted infra has low-latency endpoints, but we should run the benchmark to prove it. Also we can route by policy to lower-latency nodes for selected routes.
[04:09] Ethan Kim: How do you handle autoscaling? Our traffic is spiky with big bursts. We need predictable throughput during launch windows.
[04:15] Tomás Alvarez: Dedicated supports reserved capacity with burst pools and autoscaling policies. You can set reserved thresholds and allow short-term bursts billed differently.

[04:24] Samir Basu: Data residency — can Private be deployed in our EU cloud for GDPR purposes?
[04:28] Maya Chen: Yes, we have private deployments per region; for on-prem you'd control residency entirely.

[04:33] Priya Nair: A practical question: our current stack uses TGI in some places for custom kernels. Any gotchas migrating model artifacts to Redwood? We have custom LoRA weights and some HF-safe artifacts.
[04:45] Liam O'Connor: We commonly ingest HF and TGI formats; LoRA is supported via adapter application during model onboarding. For custom kernels, sometimes operator-level optimizations don't port, but we can reproduce performance with our kernel selection and quantization steps. We do a compatibility pass and run microbenchmarks to identify gaps.
[05:02] Ethan Kim: For eval parity, what metrics should we align on? We use BLEU-ish for retrieval, F1 for extraction, and a heuristic 'business acceptance' score from product managers.
[05:12] Anika Rao: We'll recommend: token-level divergence, semantic similarity (embedding-based), function-calling success rate, latency p95/p99, and human acceptability on a sample. We can orchestrate A/B comparisons and provide per-case diffs.

[05:28] Priya Nair: Any risks around hallucinations when moving off OpenAI? Our legal folks will ask if model behaviors can become less predictable.
[05:36] Liam O'Connor: Hallucinations are model-dependent; if you choose the same base model family and tune similarly, differences usually shrink. But sometimes instruction-tuning variants or different sampling defaults cause variance. Our rollout tooling supports canarying with automatic fallback to OpenAI for a short period if needed.

[05:56] Rosa Martinez: A nitty-gritty: we have 32k-context flows for documents ingestion. How does Redwood handle long context with KV caches across multi-GPU?
[06:05] Liam O'Connor: We support sharded KV caches and cross-GPU routing; our runtime keeps KV locality to reduce cross-host traffic and offers streaming chunk optimization. For 32k windows, the hardware sizing matters; we can provide recommended cluster sizes and expected token throughput for your prompt mixes.

[06:26] Ethan Kim: What's the cheapest path to get started? We want to prove parity before a big contract.
[06:31] Maya Chen: Typical path: 1) Hosted pilot running your prompt suite for 2-3 weeks to measure parity, 2) move to Dedicated reserved capacity for scale tests, 3) Private if you need VPC/air-gapped. For the pilot, we can provide initial free credits and help run the benchmark.

[06:46] Priya Nair: On billing and cost transparency, we need token-level breakdowns per route and ability to cap spend.
[06:52] Tomás Alvarez: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per model/route and quota controls; we can also set hard spend caps and alerts.

[07:02] Samir Basu: SSO and provisioning — you said SAML? Can we integrate with Okta and have per-team RBAC?
[07:07] Maya Chen: Yes SAML/Okta and role-based controls are supported, and we offer SCIM for user sync in enterprise plans.

[07:15] Ethan Kim: A couple of quick clarifications: do you support streaming with the same semantics as OpenAI? And what about function calling where the model returns nested JSON?
[07:25] Anika Rao: We support streaming and try to match OpenAI's chunking behaviour; complex nested JSON from functions is supported and we provide validators/parsers. Occasionally stream chunk boundaries differ slightly—another reason to run the parity test.

[07:40] Maya Chen: We're getting close to time. Quick recap and proposed next steps?
[07:45] Priya Nair: From our side: we'll share the golden prompt sets and the success criteria for parity. We want the benchmark to include function-calling cases, streaming, and long-context doc summarization.
[07:55] Ethan Kim: Also include the TGI/vLLM configs we have so you can try matching them.
[08:00] Maya Chen: Great. From Redwood: we'll send SOC2 + ISO docs, a benchmarking plan and scripts, propose a Hosted pilot and a Dedicated sizing estimate and ballpark pricing. We'll also schedule a week-of deep dive on quantization and multi-GPU KV cache with your infra team.
[08:18] Samir Basu: Can you include HSM/KMS integration notes? We need to know how keys are managed in Private mode.
[08:24] Anika Rao: Yes we will include KMS/HSM integration docs and key governance model for Private.

[08:30] Priya Nair: Rough timeline — we want to run the pilot by mid-November and decide on Dedicated/Private by December if parity looks good.
[08:37] Maya Chen: Sounds doable. We'll follow up with scheduling and artifacts in the next 48 hours.

[08:43] Priya Nair: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[08:45] Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with next steps, and Liam will take lead on the benchmark.

[08:50] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: speaker overlaps, occasional mis-heard acronyms (vllm -> v-l-l-m, TGI -> tee-gee-eye), and minor punctuation errors.
